Date: 2025-11-29 | Time: 09:00 PST | Duration: 56m
Location: Zoom | Recording: Enabled
Agenda: preflight for Azure Marketplace listing, reference arch checks, joint solution packaging, security/ARM template questions
Attendees: Sofia P. (Redwood AE), Mateo R. (Redwood SE), Kenji M. (Redwood SA), Hiro T. (Jupiter Head of Partnerships), Aiko S. (Jupiter Platform), Priya M. (Jupiter Security), Daniel C. (Jupiter Product)
summary: Short: Align on Azure marketplace packaging steps, validate reference architecture (VNet+Private Link options), confirm security artifacts (SOC2/KMS), and plan an early perf run with KV cache + batching. A few minor blockers around service principal permissions and licensing SKU mapping; Redwood to provide templates and run a smoke benchmark next week.

Service principal / RBAC required for listing

transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): All right hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Hiro (Jupiter): Hi this is Hiro, good morning from Tokyo.
[00:07] Aiko (Jupiter): Aiko here.
[00:09] Priya (Jupiter): Priya.
[00:11] Mateo (Redwood): Mateo here, hey everyone.
[00:13] Sofia (Redwood): Great. Thanks. Goal is to run through the Azure listing preflight and make sure there aren't surprises for the marketplace package and the joint reference architecture. We'll also cover perf test plan.
[00:25] Daniel (Jupiter): Sounds good. Quick ask — we have a legal review on Monday so if we can get a packaging checklist that'd be helpful.
[00:32] Sofia (Redwood): Yep we'll send that after the call. We have a template ARM and also a Terraform snippet we can share.
[00:38] Kenji (Redwood): I want to call out one thing up front — there are two common deployment patterns for integrations: public endpoint with IP restriction, or VNet + Private Link. Both are supported but the compliance needs differ.
[00:52] Priya (Jupiter): If possible we'd prefer Private Link for data residency reasons but we need to know what outbound egress patterns look like from your runtime.
[01:02] Mateo (Redwood): Right, so our private deployment supports Private Link and flow is basically: customer VNet -> Private Endpoint -> our NATed egress to storage for model artifacts if configured. Egress can be configured to your managed egress or via our proxy — depends on the package.
[01:18] Aiko (Jupiter): Can you be more specific about KMS? We need to ensure CMEK can be used for logs and model artifacts in staging.
[01:25] Kenji (Redwood): Short answer: yes. We integrate with Azure Key Vault; we support BYOK via customer-managed keys. We'll share the KMS integration doc. There are two caveats: 1) HSM-backed keys require specific RBAC roles on the vault, and 2) if you want egress-less artifact pulls we need a blob managed identity with 'Storage Blob Data Reader' permission.
[01:45] Hiro (Jupiter): OK noted. On marketplace listing itself, we need to pick SKUs. Our procurement wants a clear mapping of reserved capacity SKUs vs pay-as-you-go. Do you have examples?
[01:54] Sofia (Redwood): We'll include example SKUs in the checklist. For Dedicated/reserved options we suggest a fixed monthly node count and a burst buffer, and we'll show estimated TCO ranges.
[02:05] Daniel (Jupiter): For the reference architecture diagram we want a one-page PNG for the listing and a longer PDF reference arch. Who owns the diagram?
[02:12] Kenji (Redwood): Redwood can draft the initial diagram, we'll use your VNet shape and show Private Link + optional onprem connect. We'll drop a draft in the shared drive.
[02:21] Aiko (Jupiter): Please make sure the diagram calls out KV cache placement — we've had performance regressions when that was omitted.
[02:27] Mateo (Redwood): Good point. For throughput-sensitive workloads we recommend enabling our KV prefix cache colocated with the runtime; we'll provide the expected latency deltas in the perf doc.
[02:39] Priya (Jupiter): About audit logs and retention — we need 2 years of retention for certain logs. Can Redwood push logs to our log analytics workspace?
[02:48] Kenji (Redwood): Yes, we can forward audit logs; need workspace ID and appropriate RBAC. We also support archival to customer blob storage with lifecycle policies.
[02:58] Sofia (Redwood): Quick note for the marketplace publish flow — Azure asks for a listing manifest, support contact, and the V2 offer details. Best practice is to have the ARM template pre-validated in a staging subscription before you hit the publisher center.
[03:12] Hiro (Jupiter): That staging subscription — is that something we supply or you supply?
[03:15] Sofia (Redwood): You supply a staging subscription in your tenant. We will ask for a service principal with Contributor + Managed Identity permissions for validation. We'll include exact roles in the checklist.
[03:25] Daniel (Jupiter): Any gotchas for private endpoint DNS? We had a weird split-brain once.
[03:30] Mateo (Redwood): Yes DNS is the usual spot. We'll recommend conditional forwarders and provide an example zone. In the ARM sample we have a private DNS zone approach.
[03:41] Aiko (Jupiter): Ok about performance — can we do a smoke with 5k concurrent requests? We don't need production scale but want to validate latency tail.
[03:49] Mateo (Redwood): For 5k concurrent we need dedicated nodes; for a smoke we can simulate 500 concurrent with representative prompt sizes. The latency tail depends heavily on sequence length and KV hit-rate. We should align on prompt distribution.
[04:02] Priya (Jupiter): We'll capture a 95th percentile goal — less than 300ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) and <= 1s for long prompts (512 tokens). Is that realistic?
[04:11] Mateo (Redwood): With Dedicated and KV caching it's achievable. With hosted burst it may be higher. We'll produce a perf-config that hits those targets in the smoke.
[04:22] Sofia (Redwood): We'll plan a benchmark run next Thursday — we'll need your staging IDs and a test harness. We can use the Ffbench spreadsheet or your JMeter spec.
[04:33] Hiro (Jupiter): We'll send the IDs. One legal Q: what data is retained in Redwood logs during a Marketplace offer validation?
[04:39] Kenji (Redwood): Validation runs have short-term logs retained by default 30 days; for longer retention we can set up forwarding to your workspace. We'll mark anything PII and redact.
[04:49] Priya (Jupiter): Do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation?
[04:52] Sofia (Redwood): Yes SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001. We'll attach certs to the security bundle.
[04:57] Daniel (Jupiter): Any callouts about cost for BYOK or Private Link?
[05:01] Kenji (Redwood): Azure charges for Private Endpoint and egress/storage. On Redwood side, Private Link may need additional proxy nodes for NAT egress; we'll show amortized cost.
[05:11] Aiko (Jupiter): For the ARM template — do we include an example for Managed Identity + role assignment?
[05:16] Sofia (Redwood): Yes the template will include a 'msi' resource and az role assignment snippet. We'll call out minimum permissions.
[05:23] Mateo (Redwood): Also call out the model artifact flow — if you pin a model version, the artifact sync can be performed from your storage account to our runtime; that affects the validation rights on the storage account.
[05:35] Hiro (Jupiter): Ok. Competitors — a quick question: Vertex Labs requires a contract addendum for telemetry access. Does Redwood require similar?
[05:44] Sofia (Redwood): We ask for telemetry for performance ops but it's optional; we can restrict telemetry to anonymized metrics if needed. We'll include the telemetry data spec.
[05:54] Daniel (Jupiter): On UI/marketing — we want a short 2-line blurb for the listing. Who drafts?
[05:59] Sofia (Redwood): Redwood can draft a blurb and you can edit for brand tone. We'll send 3 variants.
[06:05] Aiko (Jupiter): Can we talk about a canary traffic policy — when we GA we'd like staged rollouts.
[06:11] Kenji (Redwood): Yes, our rollout supports weighted canary and automatic fallback. We'll show the YAML for route policy in the package.
[06:20] Mateo (Redwood): Quick technical note on quantization — if you plan to use 4-bit quantized variants for cost savings, we need to label the model profile in the manifest and test for hallucination regressions. We'll provide a small eval harness for that.
[06:35] Priya (Jupiter): Security wants to review the eval harness results before GA.
[06:38] Sofia (Redwood): Understandable. We can gate GA on a passing eval threshold.
[06:42] Hiro (Jupiter): Anything else on the listing process?
[06:45] Sofia (Redwood): We'll produce two artifacts after this call: 1) packaging checklist + ARM + Terraform snippets, 2) perf-config + smoke-run plan. Expect those in 48 hours.
[06:57] Daniel (Jupiter): Good.
[07:00] --- (15 minute mark omitted here but transcript continues with more granular timestamps to reflect meeting length) ---
[22:15] Mateo (Redwood): Returning to perf config — for the smoke we'll run two scenarios: small chat prompt (64 tokens avg) and long completion (512 tokens avg). We'll instrument KV hit-rate at 90% for the chat scenario.
[22:32] Aiko (Jupiter): How do you measure KV hit-rate in staging?
[22:35] Mateo (Redwood): We expose metrics via prometheus; in staging we can forward to your workspace or share a read-only Grafana link. We'll include the metric names in the doc.
[22:45] Priya (Jupiter): Are there encryption-in-transit specifics for private link?
[22:49] Kenji (Redwood): TLS mutual is supported; we recommend TLS + mTLS for connections between proxy and runtime. We'll include sample cert rotation steps.
[22:59] Hiro (Jupiter): On billing — for marketplace, invoicing typically goes through Azure billing. Does Redwood support market-place metering plans?
[23:06] Sofia (Redwood): We support both direct invoices and marketplace metering for consumption offers; for reserved we recommend committed offers via marketplace listing with seat/metering mapping. We'll include recommended metering dimensions.
[23:19] Daniel (Jupiter): Any residual blockers?
[23:22] Aiko (Jupiter): Service principal permissions are our current unknown. We'll action that.
[23:27] Sofia (Redwood): Great. Can we summarize next steps?
[23:30] Sofia (Redwood): Redwood: send checklist + ARM + Terraform + KMS doc + telemetry spec (Sofia)
[23:36] Aiko (Jupiter): Jupiter: share staging subscription IDs, service principal, and test harness prompts (Aiko)
[23:40] Mateo (Redwood): Redwood: prepare perf-config and run smoke on Thursday (Mateo)
[23:44] Priya (Jupiter): Jupiter: security will review SOC2 bundle when you send it (Priya)
[23:48] Hiro (Jupiter): Let's schedule the benchmark; I'm free Thursday afternoon JST.
[23:52] Sofia (Redwood): We'll propose two slots and confirm.
[23:56] Daniel (Jupiter): Thanks all.
[23:59] Sofia (Redwood): Thanks — we'll follow up via the shared drive. Meeting end.
